simon: Ran an apples-to-apples run on the replay harness comparing rv1-medium (float) vs rv1-medium-4bit (quant). Repro steps below and the weird part: p95 latency for the quant build is ~22% higher even though GPU util is lower.

elaine: can you paste the exact command + kernel selection log (the selector prints are super helpful) ?

simon: sure. command i used:
```
./tools/replay_runner --model rv1-medium-4bit --replay-id 20260301-prod-10k --decode "temp=0.0,top_p=0.95,stop=\"\"" --tokenizer utf8-strict --kernels auto --batcher continuous --affinity gpu0 --profile=perf
```
kernel selection excerpt from runtime log:
```
[2026-03-12T14:12:03Z] kernel_selector: avg_seq_len=46.7 histogram_peak=48 selected_kernel=fused_gemm32 quant_path=fp4_fused_gemm32 fallback=none
[2026-03-12T14:12:03Z] kv_cache: warmed_prefix=false kv_hit_rate_est=0.62
[2026-03-12T14:12:03Z] batcher: continuous batch_sz=1..16 target_latency_ms=25
```

ben: interesting — selector picked fused_gemm32 which is generally faster for long seqs, but quant path might introduce extra gather/scatter overhead when KV cache misses happen. Did you verify tokenizer alignment (same token counts / stop handling) between the two builds?

simon: yes, i ran a token parity check on the 100-sample prompt set: counts identical, stop token behavior matched. sample: 
```
prompt: "Summarize the following support thread..."\ntokens: [34, 256, 98, 12, 2]
```

nina: can we repro on dedicated? @ops-bot can you spin a repro pool (same hw as CI)?

ops-bot: starting dedicated pool "repro-quant-8xA100" (8xA100, 64GB) for job=jr-8831. ETA 90s.

elaine: also try forcing the kernel selector to consider kv_hit_rate: `--kernels 'force:split-gemm'` and rerun apples. when we last saw this pattern, split-gemm kept latency stable but reduced p95 variance.

perf-bot: perf alert: regression detected on branch feature/quant-kernel (commit ab12c3f). p99 increased 1.8x for rv1-medium-4bit vs baseline. Top diff: more small kernels invoked (scatter/gather) causing driver overhead.

ben: my hypothesis: decoding params + stop handling shift sequence distribution toward longer tails (more likely to hit borderline seq lengths). selector heuristics use mean/median; needs to consider tail percentiles or kv_warmup. propose we add kv_warmup pass in replay harness to prefill prefix caches.

simon: agreed. next runs:
1) replay with `--kv-prefill=true --kv-warmup-steps=8`
2) force kernel `--kernels force:split-gemm`
3) continuous vs fixed batching: `--batcher continuous` and `--batcher fixed,max_batch=8`
collect: p50/p95/p99, kernel-switch counts, kv_hit_rate, GPU SM util.

elaine: also capture timeline with `--profile=timeline` and nvprof counters (sm_efficiency, l2_hit_rate). paste the command we expect ops to run in CI so we can reproduce locally.

simon: pasted below — i'll start the prefill + forced-split run once the pool is ready:
```
./tools/replay_runner --model rv1-medium-4bit --replay-id 20260301-prod-10k --decode "temp=0.0,top_p=0.95,stop=\"\"" --tokenizer utf8-strict --kernels "force:split-gemm" --batcher fixed,max_batch=8 --kv-prefill true --kv-warmup-steps 8 --profile timeline --export-metrics /tmp/repro-metrics.json
```

ben: if the forced split fix improves p95 by >10% we can add a selector feature flag to consider kv_hit_rate and tail quantiles. also add unit test in selector harness that simulates mixed prefix/prompt ratios.

nina: thanks — pls tag me when results are in. :mag: :chart_with_upwards_trend:

ops-bot: pool repro-quant-8xA100 ready (id jr-8831). simon: your job queued.

simon: queued and running now. i'll post the metrics dump when finished. thanks everyone. :rocket:
